chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), regarding the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High:
And whoever is blind in this [world], he shall (also) be blind in the Hereafter; and more erring from the way.

He (AS) said: He who is not guided by the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, and the revolution of the celestial spheres, the sun and the moon, and the wondrous signs, to know that there is something greater behind all that, then he is blind in the Hereafter and more erring from the way. He (AS) added: He is blind and more erring from the way regarding what he did not see [with his own eyes].
ai.seo_question: What does it mean to be 'blind in the Hereafter' according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In *Al-Tawhid*, Shaykh al-Saduq cites Imam al-Baqir (AS) to interpret the verse as a warning against failing to use rational observation (*tafakkur*) of cosmic signs—such as the alternation of night and day—to deduce the existence of a greater Creator. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the unity of reason and revelation, where spiritual blindness stems not from lack of sight, but from the inability to perceive the metaphysical reality behind physical phenomena.
